recognize_zh: 骨髓切片中一顆組織球的細胞質內包含多顆完整的橘紅色紅血球，右下另一顆大型組織球泡沫狀細胞質內含數個被吞噬的核碎片／有核細胞，符合噬血現象。
features: Histiocyte with abundant pale cytoplasm containing multiple intact orange-red erythrocytes
Histiocyte nucleus oval with fine chromatin, displaced by ingested cells
Second large histiocyte with vacuolated cytoplasm containing engulfed dense nuclear material (nucleated cells or apoptotic debris)
Background marrow with erythroid precursors and a fat space
Intact red cells indicate recent phagocytosis rather than hemosiderin
describe_en: Bone marrow core biopsy section shows a histiocyte with abundant cytoplasm containing multiple intact phagocytosed erythrocytes. A second, larger histiocyte displays vacuolated cytoplasm containing dense nuclear fragments consistent with engulfed nucleated cells or apoptotic debris. The surrounding marrow contains erythroid precursors and fat. Findings are consistent with hemophagocytosis; in the clinical setting of acute EBV infection, HLH should be evaluated using clinical and laboratory criteria, because morphologic hemophagocytosis alone is not diagnostic.

ddx.dx: Tingible body macrophage / apoptotic debris clearance
ddx.vs: Tingible body macrophages ingest apoptotic nuclear debris in proliferative states without engulfing intact erythrocytes.
Siderophages contain coarse golden-brown iron granules that are Prussian blue positive rather than intact red cells.
Storage cells have crinkled-paper or finely foamy cytoplasm without ingested erythrocytes or nucleated cells.
In erythroblastic islands nucleated erythroid precursors surround the central macrophage rather than being enclosed in its phagocytic vacuoles.
